title: Atomic Distributed Rate Limiting & Token Bucket in Pure PostgreSQL
realWorldScenario: To prevent external API abuse without introducing Redis infrastructure, your architect wants to implement a high-throughput Token Bucket rate limiter directly in PostgreSQL. Each tenant has a bucket with a max burst limit and a continuous refill rate.
questionStatement: Design a concurrency-safe Token Bucket rate limiter in PostgreSQL using an atomic `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` statement. Given a request requiring 1 token, compute elapsed time refills dynamically, deduct the token if available, and return a boolean indicating whether the request was allowed.
starterCode:
-- Concurrency-safe rate limit token bucket deduction
-- Table schema: (tenant_id INT PRIMARY KEY, tokens NUMERIC, max_tokens NUMERIC, refill_rate_per_sec NUMERIC, last_refilled_at TIMESTAMPTZ)
WITH updated_bucket AS (
    UPDATE rate_limit_buckets
    SET 
        tokens = CASE 
            -- If refilled tokens >= 1, deduct 1 token
            WHEN LEAST(max_tokens, tokens + (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (clock_timestamp() - last_refilled_at)) * refill_rate_per_sec)) >= 1.0
            THEN LEAST(max_tokens, tokens + (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (clock_timestamp() - last_refilled_at)) * refill_rate_per_sec)) - 1.0
            -- Otherwise leave current refilled tokens
            ELSE LEAST(max_tokens, tokens + (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (clock_timestamp() - last_refilled_at)) * refill_rate_per_sec))
        END,
        last_refilled_at = clock_timestamp()
    WHERE tenant_id = 101
    RETURNING tenant_id, tokens, max_tokens
)
SELECT 
    tenant_id,
    tokens,
    CASE WHEN tokens >= 0.0 THEN true ELSE false END AS allowed
FROM updated_bucket;
expectedConcepts: Atomic token refill calculation based on elapsed time (clock_timestamp)
Single UPDATE statement row-level lock preventing race conditions
HOT (Heap-Only Tuple) update optimization with fillfactor = 70
Zero index maintenance on frequently mutated columns
Trade-offs of database-level rate limiting vs in-memory Redis
hints: Use clock_timestamp() rather than CURRENT_TIMESTAMP because clock_timestamp() advances during a statement.
LEAST(max_tokens, tokens + elapsed * rate) caps the tokens to bucket capacity.
Why is fillfactor essential for a row updated 100 times per second?
